title: Recovery of ferrous sulfate from basic oxygen furnace sludge using waste sulfuric acid
author: Mend, Kim, et al.

steps.title: Prepare initial leaching solution
steps.instruction: In a clean beaker, mix 40 mL of waste sulfuric acid (50 % purity) with 60 mL of deionized water to obtain the leaching solution for Cycle A.

steps.title: Leach BOF sludge
steps.instruction: Gradually add 10 g of basic oxygen furnace (BOF) sludge to the diluted acid while stirring, then heat the suspension to 70 °C and maintain that temperature for 2 h to dissolve iron‑bearing phases.

steps.title: Separate solids from leachate
steps.instruction: After leaching, perform vacuum filtration to collect the insoluble residue; wash the residue with a small amount of deionized water to recover entrained solution, and combine all filtrate for the next stage.

steps.title: Crystallize ferrous sulfate
steps.instruction: Cool the collected filtrate to approximately 5 °C (acceptable range 3–8 °C) and hold at that temperature for about 5 h to induce crystallization of hydrated ferrous sulfate (FeSO₄·xH₂O).

steps.title: Prepare leaching solution for reuse cycles
steps.instruction: For Cycles B and C, mix 60 mL of the recovered filtrate from the previous crystallization with 40 mL of fresh waste sulfuric acid (50 % purity) and adjust the pH to roughly 0–1 before adding BOF sludge and repeating the leaching, filtration, and crystallization steps.

substeps.instruction: Add 40 mL fresh waste sulfuric acid.
Check and adjust pH to 0–1 (using acid if needed).
Proceed with Steps 2–4 using this adjusted solution.

description: Fig. 1 illustrates the schematic workflow of the laboratory-scale process developed for recovering hydrated ferrous sulfate (FeSO₄·xH₂O) from basic oxygen furnace (BOF) sludge using waste sulfuric acid (50% purity). The protocol consists of three sequential stages:1.acid leaching of BOF sludge2.solid–liquid separation followed by low-temperature crystallization3.cyclic reuse of the recovered filtrate. FeSO₄·xH₂O crystals are recovered independently from each cycle, and the remaining filtrate is collected for reuse in the following cycle. This configuration enables the recovery of iron as ferrous sulfate while reducing freshwater consumption and minimizing secondary liquid waste generation. The proposed recycling protocol was validated through phase analysis of both the solid residues and the recovered crystalline products, as well as by evaluating the consistency of the product yield across repeated cycles.
